comment: Cross-border terminology and language preservation — “IPS requires SNOMED everywhere” is an inaccurate basis for architecture or procurement. Equally, a permitted coding choice alone does not establish full document conformance or receiver capability. Evidence: IPS 2.0.1 Condition profile (https://hl7.org/fhir/uv/ips/2.0.1/StructureDefinition-Condition-uv-ips.html), machine-readable profile (https://hl7.org/fhir/uv/ips/2.0.1/StructureDefinition-Condition-uv-ips.json), FHIR R4 binding strengths (https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#strength). Checked against the published 2.0.1 snapshot, including the referenced CodeableConcept profile; this is not an assertion that a comprehensive WHO-FIC IPS implementation guide has already been published.

public.suggestedRevision: Replace bullet: • Terminology and language services should preserve original codes, expressions, releases, and clinical context while enabling interpretation in the receiving clinician's language. Where an additional representation is needed for the receiving profile, it should be explicitly linked to the source and its equivalence or loss of detail documented. A terminology conversion should not be imposed where direct ICD-11 coding meets the agreed profile and use-case requirements.
